lines.japanese: 祥玄社の入っているビジネスビルの地上１階。だだっ広い吹き抜けの底にて、友人の到着を待つ鷲介くん。
lines.english: On the ground floor of the office building that housed Shogensha, at the bottom of its cavernous atrium, young Shusuke waited for his friend to arrive.

lines.japanese: ガラス越しに見る土曜のオフィス街はゴーストタウンのごとく人通り少なく、植え込みの潅木を揺らす風の音さえここまで聞こえてきそうです。
lines.english: Through the glass, the Saturday office district looked like a ghost town. So few people passed that one could almost hear the wind stirring the shrubs outside.

lines.japanese: 俺は隅っこのコーヒーテーブルに入口側を向いて座り、頂いたばかりの本を開いておりました。
lines.english: I sat at a coffee table in the corner, facing the entrance, and opened the book I had just received.

lines.japanese: まだ５ページちょっと目を通したところですけどね、なかなか面白いんですよ、これが。
lines.english: I'd only made it a little over five pages in, but you know what? It was pretty interesting.

lines.japanese: のっけから過激な性描写で始まり、毒気あるのに憎めないユーモラスな語り口で豊胸手術にまつわる悲喜こもごもを語りつつ、初めての現場に向かうロケバスでの心情をセンチメンタルに綴って一区切り。
lines.english: It opened with a graphic sex scene, moved into a tart but impossible-to-dislike comic account of the joys and sorrows surrounding breast augmentation, then rounded off the section with a sentimental description of her feelings aboard the location van carrying her to her first shoot.

lines.japanese: ふむふむ。すぐ読みおわっちゃいそうだし、誉めるのにも困らないみたいだし、これはおいしい仕事をもらったなあ。
lines.english: Hmm, hmm. I'd finish this in no time, and it looked like finding things to praise would be easy too. Man, I'd landed myself a sweet little job.

lines.japanese: ふと次の章へうつる前に頭を上げると、やたら脚の長い美男子がのたのたやってくるところでした。
lines.english: I looked up before moving on to the next chapter and found an absurdly long-legged handsome man shambling toward me.

lines.japanese: 彼は無言のままジャケットを脱いで、俺の向かいの席にどすんと腰を下ろしました。
lines.english: Without a word, he removed his jacket and dropped heavily into the chair opposite mine.

lines.japanese: 「えーと……遅かったね？」
lines.english: “Um... took you a while, huh?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、先に帰っててよかったのに。俺、行くとは言ったけど、待ってろとは言ってないよ」
lines.english: “Oh. You could've gone home. I said I'd come; I never told you to wait.”

lines.japanese: 悪びれもせず、むしろ逆ギレ気味な態度。そらまあ、言ってることは間違ってないですけど──ええ、まあ、これがカケルくんという男の子なんです。
lines.english: Not a trace of remorse—if anything, he seemed faintly offended with me. Granted, nothing he had said was technically wrong. But yes: this was Kakeru.

lines.japanese: このようにして彼は、あの見えざる敵対勢力を築いてきたのでしょう。でも俺は、彼がただの照れ屋さんだと思っているので（思いたいじゃないですか）いちいち腹を立てたりはしません。
lines.english: So this was how he'd built up that invisible army of enemies. But I figured he was just shy (you want to believe that, right?), so I wasn't going to get mad at every little thing.

lines.japanese: 「や、気にしないで。待つってより読書してただけだし」
lines.english: “Don’t worry about it. I wasn’t so much waiting as reading.”

lines.japanese: そう言ってハードカバーを立てて見せ、無為に時間を過ごしていたわけじゃないことをアピールしてあげます。どうよコレ。優しいでしょ？
lines.english: I held up the hardcover to show him I hadn't just been sitting around doing nothing. How's that? Nice of me, right?

lines.japanese: 「きのうオールでさ。や、ツルんでた連中がいろいろ面倒起こしちゃって大変だったんだよね。今日は今日で、夜ンなったらひとイベントありそうだし。俺、いつ寝りゃいいんだよ」
lines.english: “I was out all night. The guys I was with caused all kinds of trouble, and dealing with it was a nightmare. Looks like tonight's got another event in store, too. When the hell am I supposed to sleep?”

lines.japanese: カケルくんは「ごめん」を省いて寝坊した理由だけ説明しました。どうやらご機嫌ななめのようです──っても、基本的にオールウェイズ機嫌悪げなんで、ちょっと分かりにくいですけどね。
lines.english: Kakeru omitted the apology and supplied only the reason he had overslept. He appeared to be in a foul mood—though since he looked more or less permanently ill-tempered, it was rather hard to tell.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、素敵だわ。カケルくんったらお友達の面倒見がいいのね」
lines.english: “How lovely. Kakeru, you take such good care of your friends.”

lines.japanese: 彼がそんな言葉で気を良くするはずはないんですが、ご存知のとおり、俺は気が付いた他人の美徳はすぐ口にしたくなるタチなのです。
lines.english: It wasn't like that was going to cheer him up, but as you all know, I'm the kind of guy who has to say something whenever I spot one of somebody's good points.

lines.japanese: 「や、そんなんじゃなくて。あいつら、ハナっから俺だのみで無計画に暴れ放題……ま、いいや。シュウちゃんには関係ない話だよ」
lines.english: “That's not what happened. Those idiots went wild without a plan because they expected me to deal with everything... Whatever. It's got nothing to do with you, Shu.”

lines.japanese: 「えーなに、その面白げなエピソード予告編。教えてくれたっていーんじゃないの、待たせた相手にぐらいさー」
lines.english: Huh? What's with the teaser for that juicy-sounding story? C'mon, you could at least tell the guy you kept waiting.

lines.japanese: 「待ってたんじゃなくて本読んでただけ、つったじゃん」
lines.english: “You said you weren’t waiting. You were reading.”

lines.japanese: 「ま、それはそれとしてさ。ほら、事実は小説よりストレンジ？」
lines.english: “Well, putting that aside. You know what they say: fact is stranger than fiction?”

lines.japanese: しかしながらカケルくんは、突撃レポーターの追及をかわす芸能人みたいに無言で手を振るだけでした。
lines.english: Kakeru merely waved me off in silence, like a celebrity evading an ambush reporter.

lines.japanese: ひとが何かを言いかけてやめるとき、本当は聞いてもらいたいがゆえってこともあるものですが、この場合はそういうわけでもなさそうです。
lines.english: Sometimes when somebody starts to say something and trails off, it's really because they want you to ask. Didn't seem like that was the case here, though.

lines.japanese: かと言っていきなり口をつぐむのもそれはそれで空気が悪くなりそうなので、俺はあいだを取って、少しだけ話題を逸らすことにしました。
lines.english: But suddenly clamming up would make things awkward too, so I split the difference and nudged the subject sideways a little.

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに、そのお友達ってどーゆーアレ？」
lines.english: “By the way, what’s the deal with these friends of yours?”

lines.japanese: なんとなくそんなことを尋ねたのは、米田さんの口にしていた噂が意外と気になっていたからかもしれません。
lines.english: Perhaps I asked because Yoneda’s mention of those rumors had stayed with me more than I expected.

lines.japanese: 「アレって、なにが」
lines.english: “What sort in what sense?”

lines.japanese: 「なに繋がり？　ガッコー時代の同級生とか、仕事仲間のハンサムとか？」
lines.english: “How do you know them? Old classmates? Handsome colleagues, or...?”

lines.japanese: 「とか？言われても。いろいろいるから、んな、いちいち」
lines.english: “‘Or’? There are all kinds. I'm not going to list every last—”

lines.japanese: あ、言いたくなさそうですねこりゃ。またの機会にしましょう。
lines.english: Ah, yeah, he really didn't want to talk about it. Maybe next time.

lines.japanese: 「カケルさんったらお友達が多いのね。それはとても素敵なことだわ」
lines.english: “My, Kakeru, you have so many friends. What a wonderful thing.”

lines.japanese: 「世の中には虎の威を借りたがる狐が多いってことでしょ」
lines.english: “It means the world’s full of people who want to throw someone else’s weight around.”

lines.japanese: 「いやだわ。それは有名人ゆえの被害妄想じゃないかしら」
lines.english: “Dear me. Perhaps fame has given you a persecution complex.”

lines.japanese: 終始うつむきがちだったカケルくんが、ゆっくり頭をもたげました。
lines.english: Kakeru, whose head had remained bowed throughout, slowly raised it.

lines.japanese: 「シュウちゃんって……平和だよね」
lines.english: “Shu... you're awfully peaceful, aren't you?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いま溜息ついた？」
lines.english: “Did you just sigh?”

lines.japanese: 「なんていうか、平和讃歌が具現化したみたいな存在？」
lines.english: “How should I put it? You're like a hymn to peace made flesh.”

lines.japanese: 「ついたよね、フッて。鼻でブレスしたよね」
lines.english: “You did. You went ‘hff’ through your nose.”
“Oh.”

lines.japanese: 逃げるように横を向いたカケルくんが、ぼそりと一言つぶやきました。
lines.english: Kakeru turned away as if in flight and muttered a single word.

lines.japanese: 「タマイズミだ」
lines.english: “Tamaizumi.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 不意に飛びだしたそれは覚えたての人名。
lines.english: The name came without warning, though I had only just learned it.

lines.japanese: カケルくんの視線を追って首を４５度曲げれば、わりと空いてるカフェの一席に、読書に耽るひとりの綺麗な娘さんがおりました。
lines.english: I followed his gaze, turning my head forty-five degrees, and saw a beautiful young woman absorbed in a book at a table in the largely empty café.

lines.japanese: 見た感じビジネス街に溶けこむにはまだ早い若さですが、白いティーカップにそっと口をつける姿そこだけを切りとって見れば、実に絵になる美少女の午後といった体です。
lines.english: She looked too young to blend naturally into the business district. Yet frame only the sight of her delicately touching a white teacup to her lips, and there it was: a beautiful girl's afternoon, ready for the camera.

lines.japanese: コンサバって言うんでしょうか、キレイ目の服装。ノンフレームの眼鏡が似合う知的な面立ち。控えめにシャギーされた毛先は、肩のあたりで揃いすぎず不揃いすぎず、なんとも絶妙な塩梅です。
lines.english: Conservative, I guess you'd call it—a clean, polished look. Rimless glasses that suited her intelligent features. The lightly feathered ends of her hair fell around her shoulders, not too even and not too uneven. Just the perfect balance.

lines.japanese: 彼女はまっすぐ背筋を伸ばした、ともすれば見てる方が疲れてきそうな姿勢で、テーブルすれすれに浮かせた文庫本へと目を落としておりました。
lines.english: Her back was perfectly straight—so straight that watching her could become tiring—and she lowered her eyes toward a paperback held just above the table.

lines.japanese: かっちりした折り目正しいそのさまは、ポストモダン建築の高層ビルにそそぐ柔らかな晩秋の陽射しを受けて、きりりと崇高でやんごとない雰囲気を漂わせています。
lines.english: Beneath the soft late-autumn sunlight spilling through the postmodern high-rise, her prim, impeccable figure possessed a crisp and almost aristocratic dignity.

lines.japanese: 「え、タマイヅミってたしか……」
lines.english: “Wait, Tamaizumi was...”

lines.japanese: 俺は椅子の上で自分のバッグを開き、しまったばかりの本を慌てて引っぱりだして──
lines.english: I opened my bag on the chair, hurriedly pulled out the book I had just put away, and—

lines.japanese: 「多摩いづみ！？」
lines.english: “Izumi Tama?!”

lines.japanese: ──表紙に書かれていた著者名を、声に出して読みあげました。
lines.english: —read the author’s name aloud from the cover.

lines.japanese: 「あれが……や、あちらの方が？」
lines.english: “That girl... sorry, that young lady?”

lines.japanese: 俺が驚いたのは偶然の出会いにというより、その予想に反するいづみ先生のお姿にです。
lines.english: What surprised me wasn't so much running into her by chance as seeing Izumi looking nothing like I'd expected.

lines.japanese: や、そんな予想とかべつにしてたわけではないんですけど、およそ経歴や作風からイメージしうるジャラジャラした女性像からは掛けはなれていました。
lines.english: Not that I had entertained any particular picture of her. Even so, she stood worlds apart from the gaudy, jangling sort of woman one might imagine from her career and prose.

lines.japanese: なにしろご覧の通り、いまテーブルみっつ隔てた席で静かに読書しているその少女は、グランドピアノやゴールデンレトリバーの似合ういいとこのお嬢さん（お嬢様まではいかない）って感じなのです。
lines.english: As you can see, the girl quietly reading three tables away looked like a young lady from a good family—though not quite an heiress—who belonged beside a grand piano and a golden retriever.

lines.japanese: 「やー、びっくり。ほーんと、人間って生き物は実に奥が深いわあ」
lines.english: My, what a surprise. People really are full of hidden depths, aren't they?

lines.japanese: 英字新聞柄のブックカバーが似合うその理知的なお姿を眺めながら、彼女の波乱に満ちた人生を５ページ分だけでもオーバーラップさせると、なんてゆーか一言では表せない感慨深いものがあります。
lines.english: Watching her sit there looking so intellectual, with that English-newspaper book cover suiting her perfectly, and laying even those first five pages of her turbulent life over the image... well, it left me feeling something I couldn't quite put into words.

lines.japanese: ていうか、繰りかえしますけど若いです彼女。俺と同じぐらい、いや、むしろ年下に見えるんですけど……ま、職歴を考えると流石にそれはないですよねぇ。
lines.english: I mean, I know I'm repeating myself, but she looked young. About my age—maybe even younger. Though given her work history, that obviously couldn't be right.

lines.japanese: 「なに、シュウちゃんもタマイズミ知ってんの？」
lines.english: “What, Shu? You know Tamaizumi too?”

lines.japanese: 「あ……ううん、知らなかったけど、さっき読みはじめた」
lines.english: “Oh... no, I didn’t. But I started reading her just now.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 例の青い表紙を見せると、カケルくんは一度ぽかんとして──
lines.english: When I showed him the blue cover, Kakeru stared blankly for a moment—

lines.japanese: 「ああ……ああ、それか」
lines.english: “Oh... Oh, that.”

lines.japanese: ──しかし、すぐ納得できたように薄く笑いました。
lines.english: —then smiled faintly, as if everything had become clear.

lines.japanese: 「え、カケルくんこそ、彼女とはお仕事かなんかで？」
lines.english: “How do you know her, Kakeru? Through work?”

lines.japanese: ふたりを交互に指差しながら尋ねると、カケルくんは「そんなとこ」と言った感じでついっと顎を突きだしました。
lines.english: I pointed from one to the other. Kakeru tipped his chin in a gesture that meant more or less, ‘Something like that.’

lines.japanese: 「ね、シュウちゃん。あいつにサインでももらってくれば？」
lines.english: “Hey, Shu. Why don’t you get her autograph?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、そういうミーハーなのはともかく……どうしよ、一言ご挨拶しとこうかな。実はさっき、米田さんにこの本の記事頼まれちゃって」
lines.english: “I'm not really one for celebrity gawking... Though perhaps I ought to introduce myself. Yoneda just commissioned me to write about this book.”

lines.japanese: 「へえー！」
lines.english: “Really!”

lines.japanese: 「いーんじゃない、行ってきなよ。俺、ここで待ってるから」
lines.english: “Then go ahead. I’ll wait here.”

lines.japanese: カケルくんはそう言いながらも、すっと顎を引いて隠れるように表情を伏せてしまいました。
lines.english: Even as he spoke, Kakeru drew in his chin and lowered his face as if hiding.

lines.japanese: 「……はあ。つまり、ひとりで行けと？」
lines.english: “...Huh. So I’m supposed to go by myself?”

lines.japanese: 面識あるなら紹介してくれればいいのに。彼ったら相変わらずの人間嫌いです。
lines.english: If he knew her, he could've at least introduced us. Honestly, the guy was as antisocial as ever.

lines.japanese: 「えーと、それではカケルくん、参考までに聞いておきましょう──」
lines.english: “Before I go, Kakeru, let me ask for reference purposes—”

lines.japanese: せめて円滑な交流を図るため、傾向と対策ぐらいは教えてもらいましょう。
lines.english: At the very least, he could furnish me with a little intelligence—tendencies and countermeasures—for smooth diplomatic contact.

lines.japanese: 「──多摩いづみさんって、リアルじゃどんな方？」
lines.english: “—what is Izumi Tama like in real life?”

lines.japanese: 「多摩いづみ？　多摩いづみならコテコテのギャル系だけど」
lines.english: “Izumi Tama? She’s the flashy type, through and through.”

lines.japanese: 「あれで！？」
lines.english: Looking like that?!

lines.japanese: 思わず眉間に皺を寄せて見入ってしまいました。一般的にギャル系ってーと、派手めのブランドに身を固めてメンソールの細長いタバコ片手にギャハハと笑う、みたいな女性を指すと思っていたのですが……。
lines.english: I found myself staring at her, brow furrowed. To me, “the flashy type” meant a woman decked out in showy designer labels, laughing her head off with a long menthol cigarette in one hand...

lines.japanese: 「仕事のときは猫ぐらい被んじゃない？」
lines.english: “She probably plays the sweet little kitten at work.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そっか、ここにいるってことはつまり仕事で来てんだもんねえ」
lines.english: “Ah. Of course. If she’s here, she must be here on business.”

lines.japanese: たしかに俺だって、ＴＰＯに応じてアメショーとサーベルタイガーを被りわけたりぐらいはします。
lines.english: Sure, I put on my American-shorthair face or my saber-toothed-tiger face too, depending on the time, place, and occasion.

lines.japanese: 「ふんふん、ギャル系……そんで、そんで？　多摩いづみの好きな話題とか分かる？」
lines.english: “Uh-huh. Flashy... So what else? Any idea what Izumi Tama likes to talk about?”

lines.japanese: 「多摩いづみ？　そーねえ、多摩いづみだったらお硬い話とかは嫌いみたいよ。フランクに行った方がいんじゃない、軽く小ギャグとか挟んで」
lines.english: “Izumi Tama? Well, Izumi Tama doesn’t seem to like stiff conversation. You’d probably do better being casual. Toss in a few jokes.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、パーティージョークみたいの？」
lines.english: “Party jokes?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃなくて下ネタ。マスターみたいに、セクハラ入ってるベタなの」
lines.english: “Dirty jokes. The corny, borderline-harassment kind the boss tells.”

lines.japanese: 「初対面でエロポップ！？」
lines.english: “Sex-pop on a first meeting?!”

lines.japanese: 軽部狩男の無駄に渋い笑顔が脳裏に浮かび、俺は鮮烈な驚愕を覚えました。
lines.english: Karuo Karube's pointlessly suave smile flashed through my mind, and a fresh wave of shock hit me.

lines.japanese: 「え……ちょっと待って。俺、初めてご挨拶させていただくのよ？　それはどうなの？」
lines.english: Uh... wait a second. This is my first time meeting her, you know? You really think that's okay?

lines.japanese: 「いや、アリだって」
lines.english: “Yes. It works.”

lines.japanese: 「うそーん！」
lines.english: “No waaay!”

lines.japanese: 「俺んときはかなりウケてたよ、多摩いづみに」
lines.english: “Worked pretty damn well on Izumi Tama when I did it.”

lines.japanese: 「経験談！？」
lines.english: “This is based on experience?!”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょ……教えて教えて。具体的になに言えばいいの」
lines.english: “Wait, tell me. What exactly should I say?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、マスターみたいのだって。パンツ何色？とか」
lines.english: “I told you, something the boss would say. Ask what color her underwear is.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ごめんなさい、そういうのちょっとボクのキャラじゃないんで。事務所的にもＮＧですし、千歳鷲介としての商品価値が……」
lines.english: “Ah, forgive me. That sort of material is outside my established persona. My agency has vetoed it, and then there's the market value of the Shusuke Chitose brand—”

lines.japanese: 「シュウちゃん、バイトったって一応はビジネスなんだから、ペラいプライド持ちこまない方がいいって。そんなん公私混同じゃん」
lines.english: Shu, even if it's part-time, business is still business. Don't bring your flimsy little pride into it. That's mixing work and personal stuff.

lines.japanese: 「ううう、ビジネスで親父ギャグ強要されるなんて、現代の若者文化おそるべしっす」
lines.english: Ugh. Being forced to tell dirty old-man jokes for work—modern youth culture is terrifying.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、向こうも仕事用の仮面かぶってるから、遠慮してすぐにはノッてこないかもしんないけどね。大事なのはそこで引きさがんないこと。相手があったまるまで何度も何度もパス出してあげてさ」
lines.english: “She’ll be wearing her professional mask too, so she may hold back and not play along right away. The important thing is not to back off. Keep giving her openings, again and again, until she warms up.”

lines.japanese: 「セクハラ・ソロライヴ！？」
lines.english: “A one-man sexual-harassment show?!”

lines.japanese: 「辛い……それは辛いよカケルくん」
lines.english: “That’s rough... That’s really rough, Kakeru.”

lines.japanese: 「言ってんじゃん。シュウちゃんは辛くても、相手が多摩いづみなら喜ぶんだってば」
lines.english: “That’s what I’m telling you. It’ll be rough for you, Shu, but Izumi Tama will love it.”

lines.japanese: 「心配ならここで会話聞いててあげるよ。相手が本当に嫌がってるときはサイン出すからさ。これがＧＯで、これＳＴＯＰね」
lines.english: “If you’re worried, I’ll listen from here. I’ll signal if she genuinely hates it. This means go; this means stop.”

lines.japanese: カケルくんは親指をまず上に立て、次いでひっくり返して下に向けました。
lines.english: Kakeru first held his thumb upward, then inverted it and pointed it down.

lines.japanese: 「えー、そんな管制塔やめて一緒に来てよー、お母さーん」
lines.english: “Aw, quit playing air traffic controller and come with me, Mommyyy.”

lines.japanese: 俺は頑是ない子供のようにカケルくんの腕を掴みましたが、彼はそれをはらって、サムズアップしたこぶしを突きつけてくるのでした。
lines.english: I clutched Kakeru’s arm like a stubborn child. He shook me off and thrust a thumbs-up fist at me.

lines.japanese: つまり「行け」のサイン。
lines.english: The signal to go.

lines.japanese: 「ちぇー」
lines.english: “Tch.”

lines.japanese: 仕方なく、俺ははじめてのおつかいに赴く四歳児の気分で席を立ちました。
lines.english: With no alternative, I rose from my chair feeling like a four-year-old setting out on his very first errand.

lines.japanese: しかし、この世の生きとし生けるものすべてにあまねく好かれたいと思っている逆博愛主義の鷲介くんとしては、心を狩男にしてでもファーストコンタクトを良い結果で終えたいところです。
lines.english: But young Shusuke believed in universal love—with every living creature in the world doing the loving, and me on the receiving end. I wanted this first encounter to go well, even if I had to channel Karuo to make it happen.

lines.japanese: 窓の外の白い空を仰いで深呼吸。覚悟を決めた俺は気持ちを切りかえ、真面目に不真面目なネタを仕込みながらゆっくり歩いて行きました。
lines.english: I looked up at the white sky beyond the window and drew a deep breath. My resolve firm, I changed gears and walked slowly forward, preparing—with perfect seriousness—material of perfect stupidity.

lines.japanese: 「俺は狩男、俺は狩男……」
lines.english: “I am Karuo. I am Karuo...”

lines.japanese: その間、口の中でつぶやきを繰りかえし、不浄なる男の霊よ我が身に降りろと自己暗示をかけてみました。
lines.english: All the while I repeated the words under my breath, willing myself to believe: spirit of that unclean man, possess me.

lines.japanese: テーブルを挟んでいづみさんの対面席周辺に差しかかりました。俺はワンちゃん並だった速度を亀さん級にまで落とし、がしりと腕を組んで芝居がかったラウドなつぶやきをこぼしました。
lines.english: I drew level with the empty seat across from Izumi. Slowing from puppy speed to tortoise speed, I folded my arms with a flourish and delivered a stage whisper at full volume.

lines.japanese: 「うーん、目撃談だけは聞くんだけど、痴女って本当に実在するのかなあ」
lines.english: Hmm. You hear eyewitness accounts, but I wonder if female perverts really exist.

lines.japanese: しかるのち、ううむと思案に暮れるふりをして頭を傾けると、
lines.english: Then I tilted my head and pretended to sink deep into thought.

lines.japanese: いづみさんは読書体勢のまま、静かに黒目だけを上へ移動させました。
lines.english: Still holding her book in the same position, Izumi lifted only her eyes.

lines.japanese: 眼鏡の上の隙間から、レンズを通さずに俺を観察しています。煩わしげに睨むでもなく、愛想良く微笑むでもなく、ただ壁時計か赤信号を見上げるときのような感情のない目です。
lines.english: She observed me through the gap above her glasses, without the lenses between us. She neither glared in annoyance nor smiled politely. Her gaze was as empty of emotion as if she were checking a clock or waiting at a red light.

lines.japanese: つ、辛い──しかし俺は、カケルくんの助言どおり引きさがりませんでした。
lines.english: Th-this hurt. But I followed Kakeru's advice and refused to back down.

lines.japanese: 「ふうむ、やはり痴女とは、抑圧された本能的欲求が生んだ悲しき都市伝説なのかなあ。あーあ、今月の亀甲占いによれば、近日中にノンフレーム眼鏡の似合う文系痴女と喫茶店でばったり遭遇するはずなんだけどなあ」
lines.english: “Hmm. Perhaps sex-crazed women are only a sad urban legend born of repressed instinctive desires. What a pity. According to this month’s tortoiseshell divination, any day now I’m supposed to run into a sex-crazed literary type who looks good in rimless glasses, right here in a café.”
“Excuse me.”

lines.japanese: するといづみさんが、手にしていた文庫本を閉じることもなく無感情な声で言いました。
lines.english: Without closing the paperback in her hands, Izumi spoke in a flat voice.

lines.japanese: 「ご存知だとは思いますけど、思っていたことがうっかり口に出ちゃった風を装ったところで、セクハラはセクハラですよ」
lines.english: “I'm sure you know this, but pretending a thought merely slipped out of your mouth does not make sexual harassment any less sexual harassment.”

lines.japanese: 駄目じゃん！？
lines.english: It wasn’t working?!

lines.japanese: 慌てて振りかえれば、俯いて顔を隠したカケルくんが親指を下へ下へと向けていました。
lines.english: I whirled around. Kakeru had lowered his head to hide his face and was pointing his thumb emphatically downward.

lines.japanese: し、しまった、まだ早かったんだ……俺は勝ちに急ぐあまり勇み足を踏んでしまったようです。
lines.english: D-damn. Too soon. In my haste to win, I seemed to have jumped the gun.

lines.japanese: 「あ！　いやいや、これは失礼いたしました！　自分、重度の顎関節症なもので、どうにも口の締まりが悪くてははは！」
lines.english: “Oh! No, no, forgive me! I suffer from a severe temporomandibular disorder, you see. I simply can’t keep my mouth properly closed. Ha ha ha!”

lines.japanese: 「はあ」
lines.english: “I see.”

lines.japanese: 開きなおった俺は、自分を徹底的なおとぼけキャラで通すことにしました。さいわいここは出版社の真下、エキセントリックな人間も多いと米田編集がおっしゃっていました。
lines.english: In for a penny, in for a pound. I decided to play the consummate fool all the way through. Fortunately, we were directly beneath a publishing house, and Yoneda had said eccentrics were common here.

lines.japanese: いづみさんは眉ひとつ動かさず、意思の強そうな瞳で謎の男を見上げています。
lines.english: Izumi looked up at the mysterious man with resolute eyes, not so much as twitching an eyebrow.

lines.japanese: 彼女の小さなお顔には整った目鼻口が無駄なく配置されていて、その、ハイレベルな美少女にたいてい備わる特有の貫禄というか凛々しさに、ついつい圧倒される鷲介くんでありました。
lines.english: Every feature of her small face had been arranged with perfect economy. Young Shusuke found himself overwhelmed by that peculiar air of authority—or poise—that most truly beautiful girls seem to possess.

lines.japanese: や、美「少女」ってお歳でもないんでしょうけど、実際は。
lines.english: Though honestly, she was probably a bit old to call a 'girl.'

lines.japanese: 「えー、ごほっごほっ、たいへん申しおくれました。ワタクシ、フリーター……あ、いえ、フリーライターの千歳鷲介と申しますが、多摩いづみ先生でいらっしゃいますよね」
lines.english: “Ahem, ahem. I have shamefully neglected to introduce myself. I’m Shusuke Chitose, a part-timer—er, a freelance writer. And you must be Izumi Tama, the author?”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 俺はにこやかな笑顔で尋ねたのですが、返事らしい返事はなく、代わりにいづみさんの桜色の唇からは小さな驚きの声が漏れ出てきました。
lines.english: I asked with my friendliest smile. No proper answer came; instead, a tiny sound of surprise escaped Izumi’s pink lips.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ……？　ひょっとして……違い……ました？」
lines.english: “Wait... Have I perhaps... got the wrong person?”

lines.japanese: 一瞬いたずら好きのカケルくんに担がれたのかと青ざめかけましたが、次の瞬間、がたんという豪快な椅子の音が耳に飛びこんできました。
lines.english: For an instant I almost went pale, wondering whether mischievous Kakeru had tricked me. Then a chair clattered loudly in my ears.

lines.japanese: 「い、いえ！　そうです、私です！」
lines.english: “N-no! That’s me! I am!”

lines.japanese: いづみさんは本を置きすてて、勢いよく立ちあがっていました。
lines.english: Izumi had abandoned her book and shot to her feet.

lines.japanese: 「すみません！　せせ、先生なんて呼ばれたことがなかったもので、その、つい戸惑ってしまって……！」
lines.english: “I'm sorry! No one's ever addressed me like a real author before, so I—I simply didn't know how to respond!”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そーすか……」
lines.english: “I-I see...”

lines.japanese: こっちこそ戸惑ってしまうぐらい、いづみさんは丁寧に腰を折りまげて深々と頭を下げています。
lines.english: Izumi bent so deeply at the waist, bowing so politely, that I was the one left unsure what to do.

lines.japanese: それは、パッと見プライドの高そうなお嬢さんだなあ、とか思っちゃったのが申しわけなくなるぐらいの腰の低さでした。
lines.english: She was so humble that I felt bad for taking one look at her and thinking she seemed like some stuck-up young lady.

lines.japanese: 「や、そんなそんな。こちらこそ読書中に突然お声がけしちゃいまして、スイマセンスイマセン」
lines.english: “Please, please. I’m the one who interrupted your reading. My apologies, my apologies.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ！　すみません！　失礼いたしました！」
lines.english: “No! I’m sorry! I was terribly rude!”

lines.japanese: 一度は顔を上げたいづみさんがまたぞろ体育会系の新入部員みたいに頭を下げたりして、なんだかこのままじゃ切りがなさそうなので、俺は丁重に御着席を願いました。
lines.english: She raised her head only to bow again like a brand-new member of an athletic club. At this rate we would never finish, so I courteously requested that she take her seat.

lines.japanese: 「本当にすみません。なにぶん駆け出しなもので、とんだ不調法を……」
lines.english: “I truly am sorry. I'm only just starting out, and I've behaved so disgracefully...”

lines.japanese: 「いえいえ全然、ははは」
lines.english: “Not at all. Ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: お互い腰を下ろして向かいあっても、彼女はまだ肩をすぼめ気味でした。が、心なしか口元にはひそかな微笑が浮かんでいます。
lines.english: Even after we sat facing each other, her shoulders remained slightly drawn in. Yet I thought I saw a secret smile at the corners of her mouth.

lines.japanese: 初めて呼ばれたって言ってたから、もしかしたら嬉しかったんでしょうか、センセーという響きが。
lines.english: She’d said no one had ever addressed her that way before. Perhaps she liked the sound of it—being treated like a real author.

lines.japanese: 「ああもう、恥ずかしいなあっ」
lines.english: “Oh, this is so embarrassing.”

lines.japanese: 顔を背けて赤らんだ頬を両手で挟むいづみさんは、素が充分なだけにとても可愛らしく見えました。
lines.english: Izumi turned away and pressed both hands to her flushed cheeks. She looked absolutely adorable—which was easy when she already had the looks for it.

lines.japanese: や、俺もね、世が世であればね、こんなステキな笑顔のお嬢さんと、ステキな恋に落ちたりしてみたかったもんですがね──なーんつったりして。
lines.english: I mean, in another time, I might've liked to fall into a wonderful romance with a lovely young woman with a smile like that myself—ha, listen to me.

lines.japanese: 「あの……それで千歳さんは、どういったご用件で……」
lines.english: “Um... Mr. Chitose, what brings you here?”

lines.japanese: 一心地つくと、いづみさんはなかば俯きかけてる姿勢から上目遣いにこちらを伺ってきました。
lines.english: Once she had collected herself, Izumi glanced up at me, her head still half bowed.

lines.japanese: 気配りのできる俺は、彼女の緊張（してるように見えますから）がほぐれるよう、ちょっと軽めのトーンで答えました。
lines.english: Considerate man that I am, I answered in a lighter tone to ease what appeared to be her nervousness.

lines.japanese: 「あー、えっとですねー？　先生、メンズフリーズってご存知ですー？」
lines.english: Uh, well, Ms. Tama? Have you heard of Men's Freeze?

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい……ええと、祥玄社さんのファッション誌、ですよね。若い男性向けの」
lines.english: “Yes... It’s Shogensha’s fashion magazine, isn’t it? For young men.”

lines.japanese: 「そです、そです」
lines.english: “Right, right.”

lines.japanese: 良かった。女性にもわりと名前ぐらいは通ってるみたいです、メンフリ。
lines.english: Thank goodness. Looks like even women have at least heard of Men’s Freeze.

lines.japanese: 「えー、そちらの方でですね、ワタクシ、先生の最新作についての紹介記事を書かせていただくことになりましてー」
lines.english: And, um, I've been asked to write an article for them introducing your latest book...
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 「ほ、ほんとにっ！？」
lines.english: “R-really?!”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はい……あの、座ったままで結構ですから」
lines.english: “Yes... and you needn’t stand.”

lines.japanese: いちいち立ちあがるいづみさんを落ちつかせて、俺は話を続けました。
lines.english: I calmed Izumi, who kept jumping to her feet, and continued.

lines.japanese: 「それでいま先生の姿を偶然お見かけしたもので、ワタクシ一言ご挨拶をと思いまして」
lines.english: “When I happened to see you just now, I thought I ought to introduce myself.”

lines.japanese: 俺は軽く腰を上げ、改めて頭を下げました。
lines.english: I lifted myself slightly from my chair and bowed anew.

lines.japanese: 「先ほど作品の方も拝見させていただいたんですけど、これがまた、とても面白くてですね、思わず口から何か緑色の粘液が吹きでそうなぐらい……って、あの先生、聞いてます？」
lines.english: “I also had a chance to read your work a little while ago, and it was tremendously entertaining. So much so that some variety of green mucus very nearly came spraying out of my mouth... Ms. Tama? Are you listening?”

lines.japanese: 今度はいづみさん、目を丸くして呆けたように固まっています。
lines.english: This time Izumi had gone perfectly still, eyes wide and vacant.

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい！　聞いてます！」
lines.english: “Yes! I’m listening!”

lines.japanese: 「嬉しいです！　ありがとうございます！」
lines.english: “I’m so happy! Thank you!”

lines.japanese: 「や、そんな、直角に腰を折っていただかなくても──っていうか、あのほんと、座れ」
lines.english: “Please, there's no need to fold yourself into a right angle—actually, seriously, sit down.”

lines.japanese: 礼儀正しいというか、大袈裟なぐらい丁寧なひとです。新人の作家さんってみんなこうなのかしら。じゃなくて、これってやっぱり性格ですよね。
lines.english: Calling her polite didn't quite cover it—she was almost comically courteous. Were all new writers like this? No, that had to just be her personality.

lines.japanese: 彼女はちょっとお高い感じの第一印象とはまるで違う、律儀な慎みの心と微笑ましい純朴さとを併せもった愛すべき女性でした。
lines.english: She was nothing like the rather haughty young woman of my first impression. Here was a thoroughly lovable person, combining conscientious modesty with charming innocence.

lines.japanese: で──このひとが下ネタフリーク？
lines.english: And this woman was obsessed with dirty jokes?

lines.japanese: うーん、たしかに作品を見れば、そういう一面はあるんだろうけど……ほんとかあオイ。
lines.english: I mean, sure, you could see that side of her in the book, but... seriously?

lines.japanese: しかし疑いながらこっそり振りかえると、カケルくんの親指はたしかに力強くＧＯを示しています。
lines.english: Yet when I glanced back in doubt, Kakeru’s thumb still pointed forcefully upward.

lines.japanese: 「……マジっすか」
lines.english: “...Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Pardon?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いえ、なんでも」
lines.english: “Oh, nothing.”

lines.japanese: まあ、いいや。どのみち本の内容に触れていけば自然とそういう流れになるだろうし。なにしろあの激白体験談ですもんね。
lines.english: Eh, whatever. Once we got into the book, the conversation would probably head that way on its own. It was a sensational tell-all, after all.

lines.japanese: 「あの、ちょっとお聞きしたいんですけど……」
lines.english: “May I ask you something?”

lines.japanese: 「はいはい」
lines.english: “Of course.”

lines.japanese: 「その、最新作をって先ほどおっしゃいましたけど……なんで今ごろになって、あの本を取りあげてくださるんでしょうか」
lines.english: “You called it my latest work a moment ago... Why are you covering that book now?”

lines.japanese: 今ごろ……？　発行日はそんな昔だったのかしら。どっちみち編集部の意向までは聞いてないですけど。
lines.english: At this point...? Was the publication date really that long ago? Not that anyone had told me what the editors were thinking, either.

lines.japanese: 「まーほら、だって。良書に賞味期限はございませんから」
lines.english: “Well, you see... a good book has no expiration date.”

lines.japanese: とりあえずそんな風に答えておくと、いづみさんははにかみながら下を向いて、はしたなく緩みそうになる唇を口の内側に巻きこむのでした。
lines.english: When I offered that answer, Izumi lowered her head shyly and rolled her lips inward to contain the indecently broad smile threatening to escape.

lines.japanese: 喜んでます。めっちゃ喜んでます。とても初々しい反応です。
lines.english: She was delighted. Utterly delighted. It was endearing, how new all this was to her.

lines.japanese: 「あとやっぱり、ねえ、内容が」
lines.english: “And then there’s the content, of course...”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　内容ですか？」
lines.english: “The subject matter?”

lines.japanese: 「内容です。ほら、ああいう内容なら、活字慣れしてないメンフリ読者にも間口が開いてるじゃないですか」
lines.english: “Exactly. Material like that leaves the door wide open even to Men's Freeze readers unused to the printed word.”
“Is—”

lines.japanese: いづみさんの目がいったん、はるか斜め上へ泳ぎ、
lines.english: Izumi’s eyes drifted far upward and to one side.
“—that so?”

lines.japanese: すぐに正面へ戻ってきました。
lines.english: Then they returned to me.

lines.japanese: 「あの、それはどういった部分が……」
lines.english: “What aspect do you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、ええ、メンズフリーズの購買層は１０代２０代の若い男性が中心ですから。彼らファッショナブルだのスタイリッシュだの気取ってますけど、なんだかんだ言って興味あるんですよ、ああいうのって」
lines.english: “The readership of Men’s Freeze is mostly young men in their teens and twenties. They can posture about being fashionable and stylish, but in the end, they’re interested in that sort of thing.”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ああいうのと言いますと？」
lines.english: “What sort of thing?”

lines.japanese: 「ですから興味が。ネイキッド・アクトレスの赤裸々ラに」
lines.english: “I mean, they’re interested in the naked actress’s bare-all... nakeditude.”

lines.japanese: 「ね、ねいき……？」
lines.english: “Na... naked what?”

lines.japanese: どうやらフィーリング頼みの自家製英語は通じなかったようです。
lines.english: Looks like my homemade, go-by-feel English hadn't gotten through to her.

lines.japanese: 「や、ぶっちゃけ先生の作品、かなりえっちじゃないですか」
lines.english: “I mean, honestly, Ms. Tama, your book is pretty sexy, isn't it?”
“What?!”

lines.japanese: 腰を浮かしかけて、でも気が付いて座りなおすいづみさん。
lines.english: Izumi began to rise, remembered herself, and sat back down.

lines.japanese: 「え……あの本、そんなに、その……でした？」
lines.english: “Was that book really so... you know...?”

lines.japanese: 「またまたぁ～」
lines.english: “Oh, come now.”

lines.japanese: 「すんーごかったっすよ？　はじめの５ページだけでも、もうね、あのいやらしさは何事かと。現役中学生の男の子なんかが読んじゃったら、そりゃあもう春が来たかと思うべな」
lines.english: “It was amaaazing! Those first five pages alone—I mean, what was with all that sexiness? If some middle-school boy read that, he'd think spring had come.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、はじめの５ページって……書き出しの、あのシーンですよね」
lines.english: “But the first five pages... You mean the opening scene?”

lines.japanese: 「え、あのぐらいでそんな……男のひとには扇情的に映るんですか？」
lines.english: “Would a man really find something like that arousing?”

lines.japanese: 「きゃー！　言いますね先生！　あのぐらいは序の口っすか、とば口っすか、幕の内っすか！」
lines.english: “Ooh, listen to you, Ms. Tama! That was just a taste? An appetizer? The whole boxed lunch?!”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい、そんな狙いはぜんぜんなかったです」
lines.english: “Y-yes. I never intended it that way at all.”

lines.japanese: 「うーわー、くりびつ天仰もとい、びっくり仰天！　もうね、驚きすぎて言葉が引っくり返っちゃうぐらいびっくりしましたワタクシ。先生アナタはいったい、どこまで文学界のマリリン・モンローなんですか！」
lines.english: “Flabber my gast—no, I’m flabbergasted! I’m so astonished my words have turned themselves backward. Ms. Tama, could you be any more of a literary Marilyn Monroe?!”

lines.japanese: 「す、すいません、そんなつもりじゃ……」
lines.english: “I-I’m sorry. I didn’t mean...”

lines.japanese: 「はい、謝らない謝らない。アナタは全国の迷える雄羊に、愛と夢と生きぬくための勇気を与えた！　それは紙の上の悦楽園！　誇りなさい。胸を張りなさい。高らかにその８８センチの胸を張りなさい」
lines.english: “No apologies. You have given love, dreams, and the courage to live to lost rams across the nation! A garden of earthly delight upon the page! Be proud. Chest out. Hold that eighty-eight-centimeter chest high!”

lines.japanese: 「はい」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで知ってるんですか、そんなこと！」
lines.english: “How do you know that?!”

lines.japanese: 「あの、椅子倒れましたよ──や、だってほら、巻末のプロフィール欄に書」
lines.english: “Your chair fell over—well, the figure was printed in the profile at the end—”

lines.japanese: 「書いてません」
lines.english: “It was not.”

lines.japanese: あれ、８９だったかな……正直よく覚えてませんが。わずか１０ミリメートルの違いでも、女性にとっては重要なのかもしれません。
lines.english: Perhaps it had been eighty-nine... I honestly could not remember. To a woman, even ten millimeters might be important.

lines.japanese: 「や、すいません。じゃあ、こちらの記憶違いでした」
lines.english: “I’m sorry. Then I must have remembered incorrectly.”

lines.japanese: 「えーと、それではですね、作家さんの人となりを知る意味で二、三質問させていただいてもよろしいでしょうか」
lines.english: “Now, may I ask you two or three questions to get to know you a little better as a person?”

lines.japanese: 「……はい。どうぞ」
lines.english: “...Yes. Go ahead.”

lines.japanese: いづみさんが椅子を起こして座りなおしているあいだに、俺はいま一度カケルくんのゴーサインを確認しました。
lines.english: While Izumi righted her chair and sat again, I checked Kakeru’s go signal one more time.

lines.japanese: 監督は無言で叫んでいます──行けと。行きまくれと。セクシャル・クエスチョンをぶちかませと。
lines.english: The director shouted in silence: Go. Keep going. Unleash the sexual questions.
